scope: Prospective gRPC scratch diagnostic after shared header-credit and managed-admission correctness repairs in both roles. Fresh six-process corrected-control-only noise precedes eighteen comparisons; frozen protocol loads, formulas and resource limits are unchanged. No global before/after, capacity or long-test credit.

screen_policy.absolute_limits: Unchanged frozen correctness, generator validity, p99 500ms, RSS 256MiB, zero unexpected errors, payload credits, recovery and drain limits all mandatory.
screen_policy.interpretation: Descriptive resource/tail screens from three independent processes; no confidence claim for p99/CPU/RSS. Screen pass is eligibility for review, never retention or formal acceptance.
screen_policy.latency: No latency improvement required; any original A21 mean-latency regression verdict vetoes the screen.
screen_policy.missing: Any missing/nonfinite required observation is unresolved; any failed screen is rejected. No changed threshold, selected replacement or automatic retry.
screen_policy.primary: All three candidate unary allocation MiB/s observations strictly below all three interleaved control observations by more than the frozen A-only allocation range.
screen_policy.tail_and_resources: For every ordinary scenario p99, and whole-profile server CPU percent and sampled maximum RSS, candidate mean and maximum each may exceed interleaved control mean and maximum by no more than the corresponding frozen A-only process range. Applies to both profiles.

prospective_supersession.reason: Both roles add the same proven managed request-admission lifetime correction after the earlier common native header-credit correction. B17 managed JIT/AOT passed; all affected shared gates remain mandatory before new timing. No old scratch timing exists.

supersedes.reason: Spontaneous managed admission tail rejection in corrected-control AOT; no scratch timing ran. Original failed records and plans remain unchanged.

producer_identity_note: The public source has the identical tree. Actual locally built package and executable producers retain their own exact source commit; no evidence is relabeled.
